comparator.name: Bachelor Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: TU Delft's official programme and student portal, checked 2026-09-29, describe the current broad Dutch-language Bachelor Bouwkunde / Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences and link the 2026-2027 study guide. The official 2025-2026 bachelor statute identifies architectural and urban design as the programme's core and assigns 60 EC to the design learning line alone. TU Delft's published bachelor outcomes integrate architecture, urbanism, landscape architecture, building technology, management of the built environment and geo-information; they require design across scales, the relationship between people and the physical environment, sustainability, building life cycles, reuse and the synthesis of technology, design and society. The current student portal separately identifies the Bachelor 5 minor. To preserve the complete statutory 180-EC degree without inventing unavailable current course-level allocations, the comparator is represented by its three 60-EC academic years; the year notes retain the documented progression from foundations through integrated design and disciplinary deepening to minor/final synthesis.

components.name: Year 1: foundations of architecture, urbanism, building technology and design
components.note: Compulsory foundations in spatial design, representation, architectural and urban history, structures, materials, construction, mechanics and the relationship between people and the built environment.

components.name: Year 2: integrated building and urban design with disciplinary deepening
components.note: Further design studios and analytical work across architecture, urbanism, landscape, building technology, built-environment management, geo-information, sustainability and reuse.

components.name: Year 3: minor and concluding integrated design/research programme
components.note: The student portal identifies the Bachelor 5 minor; the remaining final-year programme consolidates creative and evidence-based spatial design, scientific/professional skills and integration across scales and subdisciplines.

programmes.label: Bachelor Architecture, Urbanism and Building Sciences at Delft University of Technology

exception.reason: The defining academic identity of TU Delft's bachelor is a sustained, cumulative spatial-design and building-science education. Its centre is architectural and urban design studios supported by drawing and representation, structural design, applied mechanics, building physics, materials and construction, architectural technology, urbanism, landscape architecture, geo-information and built-environment management. Design alone occupies 60 EC in the official programme framework, and the remaining curriculum integrates technical and historical knowledge into projects at building, neighbourhood and city scales. UCR offers isolated adjacent courses in sustainability, spatial planning, GIS, heritage, consumer-product design and nature-based engineering, but it has no architecture or urban-design studio sequence, no building-technology and structural-mechanics sequence, and no progressive education in construction, architectural representation or integrated building design. A 24-course UCR programme assembled from adjacent liberal-arts, sustainability and data courses would therefore remove the target's defining design-studio and engineering spine and misrepresent it as an academic match.
exception.curriculumContext: The authoritative current TU Delft sources establish a full-time, broad 180-EC bachelor organised over three academic years. The current student portal links the 2026-2027 study guide and identifies the fifth-semester minor. The latest official bachelor statute available in the public portal assigns 60 EC to the design learning line alone and describes design as the heart of the programme. Published TU Delft bachelor outcomes require integrated creative design across components, buildings, urban ensembles and neighbourhoods, grounded in architecture, urbanism, landscape architecture, building technology, management of the built environment, geo-information, sustainability, user needs and the full life cycle of buildings and urban areas. The three 60-EC year blocks preserve the complete 180 EC while avoiding invented current course titles or credit splits.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. ENSDELT111 Building with Nature provides one ecosystem-based engineering/design course; ENSSUST315 Spatial Planning and ENSENVI211 Earth Observation provide spatial engineering, GIS, remote sensing and geospatial analysis; BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design teaches a product-development studio; ENSGATE101, ENSSUST112 and ENSSUST311 provide broad materials, life-cycle/circular-economy and renewable-system content; MCCHEAM112, MCCHEAM212 and MCCHEAM315 address archaeology, heritage and some architectural history. These are useful adjacent offerings, but none is an architectural or urban-design studio, and the workbook contains no coherent sequence in building structures, applied mechanics, building physics, construction systems, architectural drawing/representation, landscape architecture, housing design, built-environment management or integrated building technology. Even using every adjacent course would not yield 23 non-PPD courses with concrete relevance to the target's design-and-building-science concept or the progressive studio formation documented by TU Delft.
